description:
We are Taha and Zachariah, dreamers & founders. 

We specialize in rapid full-stack MVP development using Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, and AI integrations.

With a strong background in platform architecture, customer success, and UX/UI, we turn complex data into accessible tools.

We are currently building "FireWatch 360". 

We would love to team up with data scientists or UI/UX designers who are passionate about Earth observation!
summary:
FireWatch 360 is an interactive web platform designed to harmonize and visualize satellite-detected thermal anomalies.
We developed a live geographic dashboard and a historical burning-activity calendar that brings together NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS observations into one accessible view.

This project directly addresses the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge by bridging the gap between raw, differing satellite feeds and actionable geospatial intelligence. 
Often, non-specialists struggle to interpret differing spatial resolutions and observation times across these sensors. 
Our platform solves this by plotting near real-time detections on an interactive Leaflet map and providing a calendar tool to compare historical detection frequencies.

This is important because making Earth observation data transparent and easy to explore empowers researchers, land managers, and local communities to identify historical burning patterns, track current thermal events, and make informed environmental decisions without needing a background in data science.
details:
What it does & How it works: FireWatch 360 acts as a bridge between NASA's raw fire data and end-users. It fetches live, Near Real-Time (NRT) thermal anomaly data via the NASA FIRMS Area API.

The application parses these CSV coordinates and plots them onto an interactive Leaflet map. Users can visually compare lower-resolution MODIS detections with higher-resolution VIIRS (Suomi NPP & NOAA-20) detections, filter by region, and use the Historical Burning Calendar to track thermal activity trends over time.

Benefits & Intended Impact: The primary benefit is accessibility. By harmonizing disparate satellite feeds into a single, user-friendly interface, we remove the technical barriers typically associated with Earth observation data.

The intended impact is to provide communities, agricultural businesses, and researchers with a clear, unified picture of burning activity, enabling better environmental monitoring and historical pattern recognition.

Tools & Technologies: We built this MVP during a rapid 24-hour sprint. The platform is a full-stack web application developed using:

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, and Tailwind CSS for a responsive, modern UI.
  • Geospatial: Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for interactive map rendering.
  • Data Parsing: PapaParse for converting NASA's raw CSV feeds into usable JSON objects.
  • Backend: Supabase (for database architecture) and Next.js API routes for secure external calls.
  • Generative AI: We utilized AI-assisted development tools (Claude/ChatGPT) to accelerate architecture planning, code generation, and UI/UX design.

Creativity & Team Considerations: Our creativity lies in the execution of the UI/UX. Instead of building a complex, intimidating scientific tool, we designed FireWatch 360 to feel like a premium SaaS dashboard.

We carefully considered data integrity; our platform explicitly separates matched vs. unmatched satellite observations and clearly communicates to users that "thermal anomalies" are not always confirmed wildfires, ensuring scientific honesty alongside our sleek design.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
